summary.text: Aisha Wahab is the Democratic incumbent for California's 14th Congressional District, having won the August 2026 special election to fill the seat vacated by Eric Swalwell. Born in New York City and raised in Fremont, she worked in technology and consulting, served on the Hayward City Council from 2018 to 2022 and in the California State Senate from 2022 to 2026. She describes herself as the first Afghan American woman elected to public office in the United States.

paragraphs.text: Born in New York, New York, and now lives in Hayward, California. According to her campaign website, she was raised in the Fremont area; she graduated from Kennedy High School in Fremont.

Earned a B.A. in political science from San Jose State University and an MBA from California State University, East Bay. Her campaign website lists a doctorate in social work from the University of Southern California.

Career experience includes working as an IT manager, IT business consultant, and senior management analyst in finance. Her campaign website says she managed operations and led large teams before entering elected office.

Before elected office, served as chair of the Alameda County Human Relations Commission and as a board member of the Afghan Coalition, Tri-City Volunteers and Adobe Services, and helped found the President's Advisory Council of the American University of Afghanistan.

Elected to the Hayward City Council in 2018, the first Afghan American woman elected to public office in the United States according to her campaign website, and became mayor pro tempore in 2020. She served on the council until 2022.

Elected to the California State Senate, District 10, in 2022, the first Afghan American elected to the California Legislature, according to her campaign website. She was sworn in on December 5, 2022, and later served as Senate assistant majority leader.

In the state Senate, chaired the Senate Housing Committee beginning in 2025, according to Wikipedia; her campaign website, written earlier, lists her as chair of the Business, Professions, and Economic Development Committee.

Won the August 18, 2026, special general election for California's 14th Congressional District over Melissa Hernandez and took office on September 2, 2026; she is also on the November 3 ballot for the full term after finishing first in the June 2 primary with 38.3%.
